summary: Phase 1 of page-level RBAC: a new shared model (`domain/shared/services/page_access.go`) lets an administrator grant a role PAGES at a LEVEL (e.g. "view", "use", "manage", cumulative -- holding a level implies every level before it) instead of editing the raw per-endpoint permission matrix directly. `DerivePermissions` turns a role's held pages into the same `AccessRolePermission` rows the server already enforces, unioning grants up to each held level and applying catalog-declared carve-outs for paths that sit under a broader grant. `IAccessRolePageService` (`role_page.go`) persists what an administrator chose (new `access_role_page` table / `AccessRolePage` entity) and re-derives the role's MANAGED permission rows in one operation, leaving any row an administrator hand-typed under "Advanced" untouched (a new `Managed bool` column on `AccessRolePermission` distinguishes the two), and `AdoptPreset` claims pre-existing unmanaged rows from installs that predate this feature so a one-shot boot adoption cannot duplicate or orphan rows. mymatasan's own catalog (`apps/mymatasan/services/pages.go`: Dashboard, Live Views, Notifications, Recordings, Objects grantable; Cameras, Detection, Teach, People, Settings AdminOnly) is proven to reproduce its existing `Policy()` catalog exactly for the viewer and operator roles, both by matrix diff and by asserting the real authorization matcher decides identically across 20 probe paths -- this is what makes adopting the model for mymatasan's existing roles provably a no-op rather than a silent widening. Building that proof surfaced a real, pre-existing gap: `/api/faces` (face enrollment) had no rule at all in `Policy()` -- correctly denied by default, but invisible in the admin UI that renders the catalog -- so a row was added there too (still no grants; admin-only).
compatibility: No behaviour change in this commit. The new page model, service, and entities are declared and unit-tested in isolation only; nothing in any app's boot sequence calls `DerivePermissions`, `IAccessRolePageService`, or mymatasan's `Pages()`/`RolePresets()` yet, and the `access_role_page` table is not yet part of any app's migration list. Existing installs are unaffected -- authorization continues to run exactly as before, off `AccessRolePermission` seeded by each app's existing `Policy()`/`EnsureRoles` path. Wiring page-derived permissions into boot and rendering the nav rail from the same page set is later work.
